intro: Armenia's ruling Civil Contract party secured a sweeping victory in local elections, while the government advanced EU partnership talks and wrestlers achieved strong results at the World Championships. Economic indicators showed continued growth alongside a state budget surplus.

topics.title: Ruling party dominates local elections
topics.text: Armenia's Civil Contract party won the majority of municipal councils in Sunday's local elections. Prime Minister Pashinyan expressed dissatisfaction with the scale of the victory, stating it created new political problems and calling for the formation of a new opposition. A parliamentary inquiry committee into the Armenian Apostolic Church also approved its rules of procedure.

topics.title: Armenia deepens EU cooperation
topics.text: The fifth meeting of the Armenia–EU joint working group convened in Yerevan, followed by talks between Foreign Minister Ararat Mirzoyan and EU Director-General Gert Jan Koopman on deepening partnership and trade diversification. Dutch Foreign Minister Caspar Veldkamp arrived in Armenia for a visit focused on transport, energy, and digital cooperation.

topics.title: Armenian wrestlers excel at World Championships
topics.text: Armenian Greco-Roman wrestlers Karen Aslanyan and Slavik Galstyan reached the semifinals at the World Wrestling Championships, guaranteeing at least two medals. Aslanyan advanced to the final, while Malkhas Amoyan and other teammates also recorded strong performances in the early rounds.

topics.title: Economy grows 6.9% with budget surplus
topics.text: Armenia's economic activity index rose 6.9% year-on-year in January–September, though growth momentum slowed. The state budget recorded a surplus of 27.8 billion drams over the same period, while foreign trade turnover increased 2.7%. The Central Bank reported a slight dip in the dollar and euro exchange rates.

topics.title: COP17 advances with new funding pledges
topics.text: At the COP17 summit, additional pledges brought Global Environment Facility funding to $4.4 billion. Armenian officials, including the Environment Minister and UN biodiversity chief Astrid Schomaker, stressed the need for science-based solutions and whole-of-society involvement in nature conservation. The UK ambassador expressed hope for practical outcomes.

topics.title: Cultural events highlight Armenian heritage
topics.text: The Yerevan Opera Theatre is set to open a new small concert hall on November 1. UNESCO headquarters will host events honouring linguist Hrachya Acharian and Republic Square. Artist Sarko Meené's works are being exhibited in Greece for the first time, while the COP17 Armenia pavilion showcases national culture in the Green Zone.

topics.title: Civil society challenges mining legislation
topics.text: Armenian civil society groups demanded the withdrawal of a bill that would weaken community oversight of mining projects. In a separate border incident, an Azerbaijani soldier who entered Armenian territory was returned to Baku, with the Interior Minister defending the handling of the situation.
